title: Communication Heterogeneity and Collective Consensus in Neural Cellular Automata
abstract: arXiv:2606.21202v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reaching global agreement from purely local interactions is a defining problem of collective intelligence, and most models of it assume that all agents share a single communication protocol. We ask what happens when they do not. Using a Neural Cellular Automaton in which a population of cells must solve the density classification task, agreeing on a global majority that no individual can observe, we introduce ``languages'' as sub-populations that read one another's messages through a translation with a tunable ``linguistic distance''. We find that linguistic distance slows consensus, that it produces mild divergence between groups rather than full fragmentation, and that a collective whose shared rule was trained under diverse protocols is robust to mismatch; a homogeneously trained one is not. translated_title: 通信异质性与神经细胞自动机中的集体共识
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2606.21202v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：从纯粹局部交互达成全球一致是集体智能的一个核心问题，大多数模型假设所有智能体共享单一通信协议。我们探讨当它们不共享时会发生什么。使用一个神经细胞自动机，其中细胞群体必须解决密度分类任务，就一个没有任何个体能观察到的全局多数达成一致，我们引入“语言”作为子群体，它们通过具有可调“语言距离”的翻译来读取彼此的消息。我们发现，语言距离会减慢共识形成，它导致群体间的轻度分化而非完全碎片化，并且在多样协议下训练出的共享规则的集体对不匹配具有鲁棒性；而均匀训练的集体则不然。这些发现在环状结构和二维网格上均成立，并且自然地可被解读为伊辛弛豫，其中外来语言的影响类似于自旋翻转。
tldr: 该研究通过神经细胞自动机发现，通信语言距离会减慢集体共识，但仅导致轻度群体分化，且多样协议训练出的系统对通信不匹配更具鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This study shows via Neural Cellular Automata that linguistic distance slows collective consensus but causes only mild group divergence, and systems trained under diverse protocols are more robust to communication mismatch.
